messages:
julia: FYI customer reporting API errors + big latency after we auto-spilled their traffic. They say requests intended for na-east-1 are landing in eu-west-1 and they see 403/token-scope errors and long RTTs. Correlation id they gave: rcid=cb7a1f2. Can someone triage?

mike: got it. Are the errors 401 or 403? Any example request/response headers from the customer?

julia: 403s. Customer pasted this curl they used and the raw response:```curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token-redacted>' -H 'X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: na-east-1' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'```Response headers: `x-request-id: cb7a1f2`, `x-served-region: eu-west-1`, body: `{\"error\":\"token scope mismatch\"}`. RTT reported ~420ms.

infra-bot: alert: eu-west-1 serving queue depth spiked to 78% of cap at 1987654280; avg token latency up 3.1x; spillover rate (na->eu) increased 22% in last 10m.

kevin: likely sequence: na-east exhausted -> router spillover to eu-west fallback. But token is scoped to na-east resources (or customer pinned region) so when routed to eu-west we return token-scope/403. Also cross-region adds latency. Possible bug: fallback routing not rewriting region-scoped auth or not applying compatible variant. Need routing logs for rcid.

sam: can we repro quickly? julia, can you run a curl from an internal machine forcing prefer-region header and capture full response + `curl -I` and `curl -v` so we get TLS / redirect traces? Also try with fresh token.

julia: customer also tried fresh token, same result. Here's a short repro I ran from staging:```$ curl -sv -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-test' -H 'X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: na-east-1' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
< HTTP/1.1 307 TEMPORARY_REDIRECT
< Location: https://eu-west-1.api.redwood.example/v1/generate
< x-request-id: cb7a1f2
< x-served-region: eu-west-1
< content-type: application/json
< \n{\"error\":\"token scope mismatch\"}```Customer RTT ~420ms.

kevin: please paste router trace lines for rcid. julia, can you pull router logs for that id (router-prod / route-decisions) and paste the entries. Look for reason=queue_exhaustion or policy=spillover.

julia: pasted logs excerpt: `[1987654282] router: rcid=cb7a1f2 tenant=acct-334 route=na-east-1 decision=fallback->eu-west-1 reason=queue_exhaustion active_shards=12 spillover_count=5`

mike: that matches. So it's not misrouting spontaneously, it's intentional spillover due to capacity. Two problems: 1) we don't rewrite or exchange tokens for fallback region so scoped tokens fail (403). 2) clients see redirect/307 + longer RTT.

sam: short-term mitigation: pin this tenant to na-east (manual override) and increase burst capacity in na-east for 30m to drain. Longer-term: router should either exchange/scoped-token-translate for fallback or fall back to a compatible model variant that accepts token scope. Also add a telemetry flag so we can count how many customers hit token-scope mismatch on spillover.

ops-bot: manual pin applied: tenant=acct-334 pinned_region=na-east-1 until=1987656235 by=sam (temporary override).

julia: customer said errors dropped after we applied pin, but they still see occasional 307s when load spikes and sticky routing key hops. They want root cause and fix, and we need to avoid billing surprises from cross-region egress.

kevin: i'll assign this to eng-runtime to inspect token translation and sticky-routing logic. Possible bug: fallback path not checking token_scope or not instructing auth service to mint compatible short-lived token. I'll dig into the router -> auth handshake.

mike: ops, can we also add a short-term circuit: on spillover, if token scope mismatch detected, route back to origin region queue (even if delayed) instead of redirecting? That will reduce 403s for scoped tokens.

sam: noted. I'll open a follow-up runbook entry for support to try pinning + token-refresh as mitigation steps.

julia: thanks all — I'll update the customer with the temporary mitigations and ask for any more repros. Will follow up when eng-runtime has a plan. :thumbsup:
